documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are solid: full VIN that decodes correctly to a 2010 Cayman S 3.4, a detailed equipment list, named private seller, location, live bid history and a Carfax snapshot showing no reported accidents and 4 prior owners. Maintenance and condition evidence is essentially absent: the seller states in writing that he has no service records beyond his own home-shop work, the 2022 PDK service and plugs are recollection only, there are no cooling-system, suspension or alignment invoices, no scan report for an actively illuminated CEL, and no borescope or leakdown. On a 16-year-old, visibly modified Porsche this is the weakest half of the category and it is empty.

condition.rationale: Cosmetically the car presents well in the photos — straight Arctic Silver panels, clean black leather, unmarked 18" Cayman S II wheels, red calipers, a dry-looking rear subframe and transaxle in the lift shot. Against that: an illuminated check engine light, non-compliant cats welded into the manifolds, Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors (unusable street pads), mismatched Michelin front / Continental rear tires of unknown date, PSS9 coilovers of unknown age and seal condition, a harness bar, and zero documentation for water pump, thermostat, radiators, bushings or clutch-side wear items at 83k miles and 16 years. Seller says no track use in his 4 years but cannot speak for the prior three owners, and the hardware set is the profile's classic track-history signature.

price_value.rationale: Bidding is $22,750 with a day to run, inside the ideal band on paper — but the profile is explicit that a PDK car with aftermarket cats, coilovers, a harness bar and a CEL is a 15-25% discount-tier asset, and that discount is already priced into where this will likely land. Layer on known work this listing itself establishes (restoring compliant catalysts, replacing track pads/rotors, correcting the mismatched tires) plus undocumented cooling and PDK service, and the risk-adjusted value is thin. Resale in 6-24 months is the weak point: a modified silver-over-black PDK with a smog problem is the slowest-selling combination in the model, not the easy flip the mission wants.

mission_fit.rationale: The mission requires a manual; this is a PDK, and it does not win the pragmatic_bridge exception because it loses on reliability evidence, condition documentation and — decisively — convenience: welded-in non-CARB cats with an active CEL make California registration a project before the car is even usable. It is also not the immediately available, low-cost, dependable bridge that the sick 335i argues for. A 987.2 Cayman S is a wonderful Highway 1 car, but this specific example is the discount, unevidenced end of it.

logistics.rationale: Greer, SC is a straightforward fly-and-drive or BaT shipping proposition and distance itself is only a cost. The real logistics problem is timing and access: the auction closes within a day, no PPI has been arranged, no Porsche-specialist inspection or scan report is on offer, and money moves before anyone can look at it. Then California smog: aftermarket cats without an EO and an illuminated CEL mean referee/registration work before the car can be plated in Carmel.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Mid-engine, hydraulic steering, Sport Chrono, LSD, a proper flat-six soundtrack and a genuinely usable two-trunk layout — the character is there and Jason likes Porsches. But Arctic Silver over black is the most common and least differentiated 987.2 combination, PDK removes the manual engagement he explicitly wants, and the harness bar, track pads and coilovers give it a used-hard tuner flavour rather than the clean, documented specialist-serviced car the profile says to buy.

positives: Correct 987.2 DFI 3.4 S drivetrain — the generation that sheds the IMS and bore-scoring anxiety of the 987.1 — with LSD and Sport Chrono, factory 320 hp.

Presents very cleanly in the photos: straight Arctic Silver bodywork, tidy black leather with no sticky-trim or torn bolster visible, unmarked 18" Cayman S II wheels, and a lift shot of a dry, undamaged rear subframe and transaxle area.
Cooperative, candid private seller who answers questions quickly and does not overstate — he openly admits he has no service records and that SC has no emissions inspections.
Carfax snapshot reports no accidents or damage, an Actual Mileage title in the seller's name, and four years / ~8k miles of stable recent ownership.
Chassis mods are quality parts (Tarett toe links, Bilstein PSS9, Soul tips) rather than junk, and the car sits and looks right.
concerns: Observed: the check engine light is illuminated and the aftermarket high-flow cats are WELDED into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO — for a car to be registered in Carmel this is a smog and registration problem requiring compliant catalysts, not a cosmetic annoyance, and the seller confirms he never pursued a fix because SC has no inspections.

Observed: PDK, not a manual. The mission requires a manual and the profile is explicit that manual commands a widening premium on 987.2 Caymans while PDK cars sell slower — this hurts both the brief and the 6-24 month resale.

Observed: the seller states in writing he has no service records other than his own home-shop work; the 2022 PDK fluid/filter service, plugs and annual oil changes are recollection only, with nothing dated for the prior 75k miles and three owners.

Observed: Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors, a harness bar, PSS9 coilovers and Tarett toe links — the exact package the profile says signals track history and pushes a car into the discount tier; the seller can only vouch for his own four years.
Observed: mismatched tire brands front to rear (Michelin and Continental) with no DOT dates given on a 16-year-old car.

Unverified: nothing on the cooling system — no water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or radiator work is documented at 83k miles and 16 years, and a bidder's direct question about it drew 'no other service records' (ask for the pump vent-hole and front radiator photos with ducts removed).
unknowns: The actual stored DTC(s) and a full PIWIS/Durametric scan, including the overrev report ranges 1-6 — the single most informative document for a car with this hardware set.
Whether the original catalytic converters/manifolds were retained and are included, and whether any CARB-legal path exists for the installed units.

DOT date codes on all four tires and the exact sizes/brands per axle.
Age, mileage and rebuild status of the Bilstein PSS9 dampers, current ride height/damper settings, and whether a four-wheel alignment was done after the Tarett toe links.
Prior-owner track history (three owners before 2022) — event logs, corner-balance or alignment records, brake-duct or harness evidence.
Borescope/leakdown condition of all six cylinders and any cold-start smoke (AOS/RMS).

seller_questions: Please post a photo of the scan tool screen showing the exact stored DTC number(s) and the OBD readiness monitor status, plus the overrev report from a PIWIS or Durametric session.
Do you still have the original OEM catalytic converters and manifold assemblies, and will they be included with the car?
You said the cats are welded into the factory manifolds — can you post close photos of that weld area and of the O2 sensor bungs?
Can you post the parts receipt (fluid, filter, gasket) from the 2022 PDK service you performed, with the date and the odometer reading at that time?

Has the water pump, thermostat, coolant expansion tank or either radiator ever been replaced? If you don't know, will you post photos of the pump vent hole area and of the front radiators with the ducts removed?
What are the DOT date codes and sizes on all four tires — please photograph each sidewall.
When were the PSS9 coilovers installed, how many miles are on them, and can you photograph all four shock bodies for seal weeping?
Was a four-wheel alignment performed after the Tarett toe links went in? Please post the alignment sheet.
Is the car currently set to the Bilstein-recommended ride height, and what damper settings are dialled in front and rear?

Will you allow a Porsche independent specialist near Greer to put the car on a lift for a borescope and leakdown before the auction closes, and can you accommodate the appointment in the time remaining?
Can you post a cold-start video from a full overnight sit, showing the first 60 seconds from behind and the gauge cluster?
Does the deployable rear spoiler raise and lower correctly with no fault, and do all door locks and the alarm/immobilizer behave normally after the car sits a week?
ppi_focus: Full PIWIS/Durametric scan: all stored and pending codes, overrev ranges 1-6, PDK adaptation values and fault memory, readiness monitors.
Catalyst/exhaust inspection: confirm what is welded where, whether OE manifolds are recoverable, and price the return to CARB-compliant units for California registration.
PDK behaviour: low-speed engagement judder, 1-2 shift delay, clutch-pack adaptation data — the 2022 self-performed service is the only claimed fluid change.
Cooling system: water pump vent hole for weeping, pink crust on the block, expansion tank seam and cap, front radiators and condensers with ducts removed for debris packing and corrosion.
Borescope all six cylinders plus a leakdown, and check the bellhousing and RMS area for oil weep and the AOS for cold-start smoke.
Suspension: PSS9 shock bodies for seal leakage and age, Tarett toe link condition and torque, front lower control arm bushings and top mounts, then a corner-weight-aware four-wheel alignment.
Brakes: measure Frozen rotor thickness and condition, confirm Hawk HP+ pad wear and any heat-cracking or bluing that would indicate track use.
Tire DOT dates and sizes on all four corners; confirm the staggered set is correct for the car.
Track-use forensics: harness bar mounting, seat rail and floor for bolt marks, brake duct evidence, rollbar drill holes, and undertray/diffuser scrapes.
Deployable spoiler mechanism operation and a parasitic-draw test given the model's known ignition switch, immobilizer and door-actuator drains.
what_would_change_verdict: It would move up materially if the seller produced the original manifolds/cats plus a specialist scan showing the only code is catalyst-efficiency, and the winning price left room for the OE catalyst restoration and street pads.

It would move up if a Porsche independent completed a pre-close borescope, leakdown and lift inspection with a clean report, and dated invoices surfaced for the water pump/thermostat and the PDK service.
It would move down further if the scan shows overrevs in ranges 4-6, misfire history, or PDK adaptation near limits — that would confirm the track-hardware inference.
It stays a no regardless if the hammer plus catalyst compliance, pads and tires puts it into the same money as a documented, unmodified manual example.
A manual 987.2 S with a specialist service binder at a similar price would displace this car outright.
evidence.mission_note: This fails the enthusiast_bridge brief on the transmission alone — PDK where a manual is required — and it does not earn the pragmatic_bridge exception, because a welded-in non-CARB catalyst setup with an illuminated CEL makes it neither convenient nor immediately usable in California, and there is no maintenance documentation to support the reliability case. In accelerated_bridge mode Jason should be buying evidence and easy resale, and this is a discount-tier, undocumented, modified car in the model's least differentiated colour combination.
evidence.rationale: This is a discount-tier example of an otherwise excellent model, and the disqualifiers are stated in the listing rather than inferred. The check engine light is on right now, caused by aftermarket high-flow catalytic converters welded into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO; the seller confirms South Carolina has no inspections and that he never pursued a fix, which converts a cosmetic annoyance into a California registration project. It is a PDK where the mission requires a manual, and the profile is explicit that manual commands a widening premium while PDK cars sell slower — bad for the 6-24 month exit. Documentation is close to nil on the half that matters: the seller wrote 'I do not have any other service records,' the 2022 PDK service, plugs and annual oil changes are his own home-shop recollection, and a direct bidder question about the water pump and cooling system produced nothing at 83k miles and 16 years. The hardware set — Bilstein PSS9 coilovers, Tarett rear toe links, harness bar, Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors — is exactly what the profile flags as track-history signature, and the seller can only vouch for his own four years and 8k miles. Tires are mismatched Michelin front and Continental rear with no DOT dates. The car does present cleanly in the photos, the underside shot of the rear subframe looks dry and undamaged, the seller is candid and responsive, and the DFI 3.4 with LSD and Sport Chrono is genuinely the right engine — but with the auction closing in about a day there is no realistic path to a Porsche-specialist borescope, leakdown and scan before money moves.
evidence.next_action: Do not bid; if Jason wants to stay engaged, post one public question asking whether the original OEM manifolds/cats are included and requesting a photo of the scan tool showing the exact DTC and readiness status, and let the auction close without him unless a specialist PPI can be completed before it ends.
